verdict.rationale: 2FAS publishes the source code for its client apps on GitHub: the 2FAS Auth and 2FAS Pass apps, the browser extensions, and a public Android repo. It markets 2FAS Auth as open-source and explicitly invites community code review, so the code that handles seeds can be inspected. missing for 10: 2FAS Pass is described as 'source-available' rather than clearly open-source licensed, and there is no evidence of an independent security audit or actual community review outcomes.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the client apps are open source, so the code handling my seeds can be inspected and community-reviewed

citations.quote: The source code of 2FAS Pass and 2FAS Auth is available on GitHub.
Join our GitHub project and contribute to 2FAS by running code review and committing your ideas.
You can easily take a look at our code - reflecting our transparent and user-first approach. Check out our GitHub repository
Source-available code ensures that every security feature we use can be verified by independent security experts.
